newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- NOV 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- NOV 29.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--The government's threats to reveal the names of well-known figures and companies involved in tax evasion is an attempt to divert the attention of the poorer classes, who are infuriated about the new economic measures. The names of the evaders are to be released to the public in the next few days. Sources say the government plans to arrest a number of the 50 businessmen.
--National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou sumbits the budget to Parliament today.
--The fall in interest rates continues with the Agricultural Bank dropping its deposit and lending rates. The Credit Bank is expected to follow suit with a more significant drop.
IMERISIA

--The government is now 'correcting' the measures announced recently, prompted by the opposition expressed by the business world and unions, as well as members and deputies of the ruling party PASOK. The changes, despite denials to the contrary, will be made to tax exemption abolitions, large family benefits and to the time other provisions go into effect.
--Dramatic fall in trading volume as problems contine to dog the Athens Stock Exchange.
--The Magic casino is to be bought by a Greek-Canadian businessmen. The new firm undertakes the casinoo's debts of six million dollars.
KERDOS

--The fate of group insurance policies taken out by 3,000 businesses for their 300,000 employees is in doubt following the government's decision to abolish the tax breaks on spending for these policies.
--The government is working towards granting productivity bonuses to middle and higher-ranking public servants as a mark of faith that incomes will not be cut.
--Monday's ECOFIN Council is crucial for Greece as Papandoniou aims to convince the EU that it will not need to impose penalties on Greece for not achieving Maastrict targets by mid-1997.
EXPRESS
--The government yesterday felt the need to issue an announcement yesterday - on the occasion of the nationwide general strike - calling for the understanding of workers and pensioners.
--A clear turnaround from the government as the finance ministry says most measures will go into effect for the 1997 financial year rather than 1996.
--Yesterday's strike was a feather in the negotiating caps of unionists. New general strikes cannot yet be ruled out.

--Private investment in energy production is a possibility with the new bill planned to be submitted in Parliament next week. The development ministry's bill will allow subsidiaries of the the public power company, DEH, and private operators to conduct joint energy production enterprises.
--State procurements contracts get a first taste of austerity.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--The fall in interest rates picks up speed, following reductions by three state-run banks. Now, the major commercial bank, Credit Bank, is expected to drop rates.
--Brokers request that the deadline for clearance of transactions be extended from 48 to 72 hours at yesterday's meeting at the national economy ministry. Four firms barred from trading yesterday.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
